title: The visible CFPB complaint-response endpoint changed over time
source_unit: published CFPB complaint record grouped by calendar year received

observations.method: Official CFPB API aggregate query for date_received_min=2020-01-01, date_received_max=2021-01-01, size=0
observations.uncertainty: No sampling standard error estimated; published-record selection and coding uncertainty remain.
observations.counterinterpretation: Later-year response shares may reflect product, routing, publication, and coding changes rather than improved or worsened consumer remedies.

observations.uncertainty: No sampling standard error estimated; published-record selection, coding, current-index timing, and the addition of an in-progress response category remain relevant uncertainty.
observations.counterinterpretation: The 2025 shift toward explanation and away from non-monetary or monetary response categories may reflect product mix, routing, publication, coding, or index changes rather than a change in verified consumer remedies.

observations.period: 2025 CFPB annual report; received → routed → company response

denominator.unit: complaints received by CFPB in 2025; rounded report count as of 2026-03-02

sent_to_company_within_one_day.unit: percent of complaints sent to companies

company_timely_response.unit: percent of complaints sent to companies; more than 99%

confirmed_relationship_closed.unit: complaints closed with explanation or relief after company confirmed a commercial relationship; approximately

observations.method: CFPB 2025 Consumer Response Annual Report, complaint data current as of 2026-03-02; annual intake, routing, and company-response administrative counts are kept separate from the published API snapshot.
observations.uncertainty: Report counts are rounded and exclude duplicates, whistleblower tips, and complaints found not actionable; received complaints are not unique consumers, and routing or timely response does not establish substantive correction, adequate relief, or household recovery.
observations.subgroup: Complaints received by the CFPB in calendar year 2025 across financial products; credit or consumer reporting complaints account for the dominant share.
observations.counterinterpretation: The gap between received, routed, and published/closed records reflects eligibility, identity, commercial-relationship, and administrative filters; the large credit-reporting volume also makes aggregate movement a data-integrity and system-use question, not a simple rise in consumer harm.

boundary: This is a trend in published complaint-system records. It is not a representative consumer sample, account-denominated harm rate, verified remedy rate, trust measure, switching measure, or causal estimate.
